verdicts.title: The OPQ-307 cross-package dependency is back in opaque-accounting's own source as an executed doctest
verdicts.reasoning: Every link verified on the current tree. packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/accounting/__init__.py:17-22 carries a live `>>>` doctest whose first line is `import opaque.dpsgd.accounting as dpsgd_acc`, followed by poisson/gaussian construction and `epsilon_at`. packages/opaque-accounting/pyproject.toml declares exactly one opaque dependency (opaque-base) and no [project.optional-dependencies]; opaque-dpsgd depends on opaque-accounting, so the edge cannot be declared without a cycle. maturin's python-packages includes `opaque/accounting`, so the docstring ships inside the wheel. .github/workflows/pr.yml:293 runs `uv run python -m doctest` on that exact file inside the docs job, which at pr.yml:285 syncs `--all-packages`, so it passes in CI. I confirmed the mitigations the finding itself concedes: root pyproject.toml [tool.pytest.ini_options] addopts is only `--import-mode=importlib` (no --doctest-modules), and grep over .github/workflows finds no lane that installs opaque-accounting in isolation, so nothing breaks today. The docstring also self-documents the requirement ('Example (requires ``opaque-dpsgd`` in the environment)'). So this is a verified latent package-boundary smell, not an active failure: the claim as written (including its own admission that ARC-006 is not violated today) holds exactly.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: No current CI lane or pytest run fails: doctest collection is not enabled anywhere (addopts has no --doctest-modules) and the only executor, pr.yml:293's `python -m doctest`, runs after `uv sync --all-packages`. The established defect is latent: the module docstring shipped inside the opaque-accounting wheel contains an executable doctest that imports `opaque.dpsgd.accounting`, a package opaque-accounting cannot declare as a dependency (opaque-dpsgd depends on opaque-accounting). Anyone who enables --doctest-modules for this package, or runs the shipped doctests as a smoke test on a `pip install opaque-accounting` environment, gets ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'opaque.dpsgd'. The docstring itself flags the requirement in prose, so this is a boundary/hygiene issue rather than a user-visible bug.

verdicts.title: The exception taxonomy inverts two pre-existing error relationships it claims to preserve, breaking except-clauses without a breaking-change marker
verdicts.reasoning: The two behavioral inversions are real and I reproduced one directly. Baseline `git show 4b13d82:.../calibration.py` line 489 is `raise RuntimeError("Calibration for {budget.name} did not converge...")`; the current tree (calibration.py:537) raises CalibrationError, which via ConfigurationError derives from ValueError only (packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/api/base/exceptions/__init__.py:27,38). Baseline `_budgets.py:311` is `raise TypeError(...)` for an unregistered budget type; the current tree raises CheckpointError, and I executed `budget_state_dict(Foo())` in the repo venv: `CheckpointError TypeError? False RuntimeError? True ValueError? False`. The change shipped in a released line, not just on a dev branch: `git describe 7b26f655` = v0.15.3-9, and `git tag --contains 7b26f655` lists v0.15.4, v0.15.5, v0.15.5.rc1/rc2, v0.15.6.rc1 - so v0.15.3 users who caught RuntimeError from calibrate() or ValueError/TypeError from the codec see those handlers stop firing on v0.15.4, and the commit subject is a plain `feat(...)` with no `!` and no BREAKING CHANGE footer. TWO CORRECTIONS to the finding's framing. (1) The docstring quote is selective: packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/exceptions/__init__.py:4-7 reads in full 'They preserve familiar Python error relationships: configuration, calibration, and privacy-budget errors are ValueError subclasses, while checkpoint failures are RuntimeError subclasses.' - it accurately documents the shipped taxonomy and does not claim the previous raise types were kept. docs/reference/exceptions.md carries the same correct mapping table. So the 'the docstring says it preserves and it doesn't' half of the title is wrong; only the silent-migration half survives. (2) This is a 0.x, Development Status 3 - Alpha library, so the release-contract argument is weaker than the finding implies. Severity stays low; no epsilon effect.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Between v0.15.3 and v0.15.4 (commit 7b26f655, titled `feat(exceptions): ...` with no `!` and no BREAKING CHANGE footer) two exception families changed base class in incompatible directions. Non-convergence in `calibrate()` went from RuntimeError to CalibrationError (a ValueError subclass, NOT a RuntimeError); the accounting checkpoint/codec sites went from ValueError, and `budget_state_dict` on an unregistered type from TypeError, to CheckpointError (a RuntimeError subclass, NOT a ValueError or TypeError) - verified by execution: `budget_state_dict(Foo())` raises CheckpointError with isinstance(TypeError)=False, isinstance(RuntimeError)=True. Downstream v0.15.3 code doing `except RuntimeError:` around calibrate(), or `except ValueError:` around checkpoint restore, silently stops catching and the job crashes instead of taking its recovery path. Mitigations: the new taxonomy is fully and correctly documented (opaque/exceptions/__init__.py docstring and docs/reference/exceptions.md both state checkpoint -> RuntimeError, calibration -> ValueError), and the project is 0.x alpha, so the only concrete gap is the missing breaking-change marker/release note, not a wrong description of current behavior.

verdicts.title: Monte Carlo shard seeds alias across nearby user seeds: seeds S and S+2 share all but one shard of the transcript corpus
verdicts.reasoning: Verified by code reading and independently reproduced numerically. packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/b_min_sep/mc.rs:34-37 is `seed.wrapping_add((shard as u64).wrapping_mul(2)).wrapping_add(direction as u64)`, and balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:50-55 is the same arithmetic with a bool direction. Trivially shard_seed(S, k, d) == shard_seed(S+2, k-1, d) for all k>=1. I checked that the alias actually propagates: the RNG is the only per-shard state, built as `StdRng::seed_from_u64(shard_seed(...))` at mc.rs:221/237/396/423 and monte_carlo.rs:205/229, and inside each `par_chunks_mut(...).enumerate()` closure `shard` is used for nothing but the seed - every other input (strategy_coef/gram, sigma, p, n_steps, chol) is shard-independent - so shard k of run S is bit-identical to shard k-1 of run S+2. samples_to_pmf sorts the sample vector (monte_carlo.rs:314), so the PMF is a function of the multiset and shared shards flow straight into the reported epsilon. Numerically reproduced against the prebuilt extension in the repo venv (b_min_sep over band_mf_strategy(bands=2), n_steps=40, p0=0.05, nm=1.0, discretization=1e-3, mc_resolution=1e-3, mc_failure_probability=1e-3 -> resolved_num_mc_samples=17354 = 17 shards): seeds 1000,1002,...,1010 give eps_at(1e-2) = 1.29801422, 1.29974058, 1.30809399, 1.31104217, 1.30283726, 1.30377245 (stdev 0.00493), while seeds 1000,2000,...,6000 give 1.29801422, 1.31705101, 1.26226398, 1.31656696, 1.33825894, 1.31136316 (stdev 0.02557) - a 5.2x collapse in spread, the same effect the finding reports with a different strategy. I also confirmed the default config really is 2872 shards (resolved_num_mc_samples = 2940252). The crate test `shard_seeds_separate_adjacency_directions` (mc.rs:710-721) only asserts within-run uniqueness, so nothing in-tree catches it. Severity low is right: each individual run still carries its own simultaneous confidence band, no reported epsilon is unsound, and the .pyi documents `seed` only as reproducibility, never independence. It degrades seed-sweeping as a stability diagnostic.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Because shard_seed is plain addition (seed + 2*shard + direction) and the shard index feeds nothing else, run S and run S+2 draw identical samples for all but one shard in each adjacency direction - at the default discretization config that is 2871 of 2872 shards, so stride-2 seeds are effectively the same estimate. Independently measured at 17 shards (b_min_sep, band_mf_strategy(bands=2), n_steps=40, p0=0.05, nm=1.0, disc=1e-3, mc_resolution=1e-3, mc_failure_probability=1e-3): stride-2 seeds 1000..1010 give epsilon_at(1e-2) stdev 0.00493 versus stdev 0.02557 for stride-1000 seeds - 5.2x too tight. A user who reruns the accountant at seeds 1000, 1002, 1004 to gauge Monte Carlo noise sees an artificially tight cluster and overestimates the stability of the bound. It also means an independently 'reproduced' (epsilon, delta, seed) triple at a nearby seed is not independent evidence. No individual reported epsilon is invalidated: each run still carries its own simultaneous KL confidence band, and the public docs promise only reproducibility from the seed, not independence. Both MC accountants (b-min-sep for BandMF, balls-in-bins for the correlated-noise MF mechanisms) share the arithmetic.

verdicts.title: dpsgd_acc.poisson() lost its inner-mechanism guard and now silently amplifies already-amplified and whole-horizon processes
verdicts.reasoning: Fully reproduced, including all four numbers, which matched to every printed digit. Baseline `git show 4b13d82:.../dpsgd/amplification/_poisson.py` has `_Inner = Gaussian | AdaClip | NonPrivate` and a factory-level `match inner: case Gaussian() | AdaClip() | NonPrivate(): pass; case _: raise TypeError('poisson() requires a Gaussian, AdaClip, or NonPrivate inner mechanism, ...')`. The current file has `_Inner = DpProcess` (:21), `__post_init__` checks only `isinstance(self.inner, DpProcess)` (:39-46), the type guard survives only inside the truncated branch (:91-98), and the non-truncated path falls through to `_native.poisson_pld(self.inner.pld(...), self.sample_rate)` (:162-173). Executed in the repo venv: `single = poisson(gaussian(1.1), 0.01)`; `(single*1000).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 1.5154423566628403`; `(poisson(single, 0.01)*1000).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.009836885508304796` (154.06x understatement, no error, no warning). `kt = k_out_of_t(gaussian(1.1), k=2, t=100, allocation='block')` gives 0.970343695110472 alone and `poisson(kt, 0.1)` gives 0.10865088995647369. The asymmetry with the DP-FTRL sibling is real: packages/opaque-dpftrl/.../amplification/_poisson.py:279-288 still raises InputTypeError unless inner is MfGaussian with a BandMf/Identity strategy. TWO MITIGATING FACTS I established that the finding does not mention. (1) The generalization was deliberate and documented, not an accident: 3b22a6af updated docs/reference/accounting.md and docs/user-guide/accounting.md to say 'Plain Poisson accepts any Opaque DpProcess as its base mechanism', and added tests for the intended use (`poisson(acc.eps_delta(0.3), 0.2)`), replacing the old `test_rejects_non_gaussian` with `test_rejects_non_process`. (2) The open-algebra footgun is not unique to poisson: I checked that `kt * 10` on a whole-horizon k-out-of-t process is likewise accepted and returns 3.0968460135957514 with no guard, so the composition layer generally lets users build unrealizable expressions. That keeps this at medium rather than high: the documented DP-SGD path is unchanged and correct, and triggering the understatement requires the user to write an expression no Opaque sampler realizes. It stays at medium rather than low because a guard that specifically existed to catch this exact mistake was removed, the failure direction is epsilon understatement, and double-wrapping is a realistic slip in helper- or config-driven pipelines.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: The factory guard that used to reject non-Gaussian inners was removed in 3b22a6af as part of a deliberate, documented generalization to any DpProcess, but nothing replaced it for inners that are themselves participation models or compositions. Reproduced on the current tree: `dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(1.1), 0.01), 0.01) * 1000` reports epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.009837 where the correct single-amplification DP-SGD figure is 1.515442 - a 154x understatement with no error and no warning, where the pre-3b22a6af tree raised TypeError. Likewise `dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.k_out_of_t(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(1.1), k=2, t=100, allocation='block'), 0.1)` reports 0.108651 against the 0.970344 the horizon process reports alone, for a mechanism ('Poisson-subsample the dataset, then run k-out-of-t on the subsample') that no Opaque sampler implements. A user who reaches that expression through a wrapper or config path and calibrates noise against it deploys at far less noise than their claimed epsilon requires. Scope limits: the documented single-amplification path (`poisson(gaussian(nm), q) * T`) is unchanged and correct; triggering this needs a user-constructed expression; and the composition layer is permissive elsewhere too (`k_out_of_t(...) * 10` is also accepted without a guard, returning 3.096846). The DP-FTRL sibling `dpftrl_acc.poisson` still enforces an MfGaussian inner, so the two stacks now disagree on strictness.
